title: Appearance Standard
summary: Every therapist is expected to maintain an appearance that communicates cleanliness, neatness, freshness, professionalism, confidence, and readiness to serve.

sections.title: The Standard
paragraphs: At Zura Spa, every therapist is expected to maintain an appearance that communicates cleanliness, neatness, freshness, professionalism, confidence, and readiness to serve.
The Appearance Standard is not simply about looking attractive or wearing a uniform.

Massage involves close physical contact. The client will notice the therapist's uniform, hair, hands, nails, breath, body odour, footwear, general grooming, and overall presentation before and during the massage.
For this reason, professional appearance is part of the service itself.
A therapist represents Zura Spa from the moment they arrive at work until the end of their shift.
Before I attend to a client, I should look, smell and present myself like a professional Wellness Expert.

sections.title: 1. Relevance of the Appearance Standard
paragraphs: Professional appearance affects first impressions, client confidence, hygiene, brand representation, consistency, and professional discipline.

sections.title: Professional First Impression
paragraphs: Before the therapist performs a single massage movement, the client has already started forming an impression.
A therapist who appears clean, fresh, neat, properly dressed, and well groomed immediately communicates professionalism.

sections.title: Client Confidence
paragraphs: Massage requires significant physical proximity and personal contact. A client is more likely to relax when the therapist appears clean, hygienic, organized and properly prepared.

If the therapist appears dirty, untidy or poorly groomed, the client may begin questioning the cleanliness of the therapist's hands, the cleanliness of the massage room, the hygiene of the towels, and the professionalism of the spa itself.

sections.title: Hygiene
paragraphs: Appearance and hygiene cannot be separated in massage work. The therapist's skin, hands, fingernails, hair, breath, clothing, and footwear can directly affect the client's comfort.

sections.title: Brand Representation
paragraphs: The client does not usually separate the therapist completely from the business.
The therapist may think: "This is only about how I personally look." But the client may think: "This is how Zura Spa operates."
One therapist's appearance can therefore strengthen or weaken the perception of the entire brand.

sections.title: Consistency
paragraphs: Clients should not encounter one therapist who looks exceptionally professional and another who appears completely different in standard.
A common appearance standard helps the entire team present a recognizable Zura Spa identity.

sections.title: Professional Discipline
paragraphs: Maintaining appearance every day demonstrates preparation, self-discipline, attention to detail, respect for clients, respect for colleagues, and respect for the workplace.

sections.title: 2. The Therapist's Mindset
paragraphs: The correct mindset is: "Before I serve the client, I must first be ready to represent the standard."
A therapist should understand: "My appearance is part of the client's experience."

Professional grooming should not depend on whether management is present, whether the therapist expects many clients, whether it is a busy day, whether the therapist feels like dressing properly, or whether the first appointment is early or late.
If the therapist is available to attend to a client, the therapist should be client-ready.

I am working in close proximity to another person. My hygiene matters. My breath matters. My nails matter. My clothing matters. My smell matters. My presentation affects whether the client feels comfortable with me.

sections.title: 3. Uniform Standard
paragraphs: The approved Zura Spa uniform should always be clean, fresh, properly fitted, neatly presented, free from obvious stains, free from unpleasant odour, free from excessive wrinkles, free from visible tears or damage, worn correctly, and complete where the uniform has multiple approved components.
The therapist should not appear as though they simply picked up whatever clothing was available.
The uniform represents Zura Spa. It should never look neglected.
list: Arrive already properly dressed or change into the approved uniform before beginning work.
Inspect the uniform before the first client.
Change the uniform when it becomes excessively dirty or unsuitable.
Avoid sitting or lying in ways that unnecessarily soil the uniform.
Keep replacement clothing available where Zura Spa requires it.
Wear the uniform according to the approved style.
Keep footwear clean and suitable for the spa environment.

sections.title: 4. Hair Grooming Standard
paragraphs: Hair should always be clean, neat, controlled, and professionally presented.

The therapist should ensure that hair does not repeatedly fall onto the client's body, fall into massage oil, cover the therapist's face unnecessarily, require constant touching or adjustment, create hygiene concerns, distract the client, or interfere with massage movement.
Long hair should be properly secured where necessary. Hair should not appear visibly neglected or unkempt during working hours.
The guiding principle is: NEATNESS + CLEANLINESS + PROFESSIONALISM + PRACTICALITY.

sections.title: 5. Personal Hygiene Standard
paragraphs: Because massage involves close contact, personal hygiene must receive serious attention.
The therapist should not rely on perfume or body spray to cover poor hygiene. Fragrance supports cleanliness. It does not replace cleanliness.
list: Bathe before reporting for work.
Remain clean throughout the working day.
Use deodorant appropriately.
Ensure underarms are clean.
Maintain fresh breath.
Brush properly.
Use mouthwash or other approved freshening methods where necessary.
Keep hands clean.
Keep feet clean.
Wear clean footwear.
Refresh themselves when necessary during the shift.

sections.title: 6. Body Odour and Fragrance Standard
paragraphs: Therapists work very close to clients. Strong body odour can immediately make the client uncomfortable.
The objective is to smell fresh and neutral, not overpower the treatment room with fragrance.
A massage environment should smell relaxing. It should not smell strongly of sweat, dirty clothing, shoes, food, cigarettes, or excessive perfume.
list: Use deodorant appropriately.
Freshen up after sweating.
Change clothing if it has absorbed excessive sweat.
Pay attention to underarm hygiene.
Pay attention to foot odour.
Avoid excessive perfume.

sections.title: 7. Breath Standard
paragraphs: The therapist may need to communicate with the client at close range. Fresh breath is therefore part of the appearance and hygiene standard.
Chewing gum should not become distracting during client interaction or massage. The therapist should never be chewing gum visibly throughout a professional massage session.
list: Brush properly.
Maintain oral hygiene.
Use mouthwash when necessary.
Use an appropriate mint where necessary.
Avoid foods immediately before sessions that cause strong lingering odours where possible.
Freshen their breath after eating where necessary.

sections.title: 8. Hands and Nails Standard
paragraphs: The therapist's hands are their primary professional tools. Clients feel them directly.
Hands should be clean, soft enough for comfortable contact, properly maintained, free from visible dirt, free from offensive odour, and free from anything that could scratch the client.
Nails should be clean, short enough for massage, smooth, and free from sharp or broken edges.
Before a massage begins, the therapist should personally ask: "Are my hands safe and comfortable for this client's skin?"
list: Excessively long nails.
Sharp nails.
Damaged nails that may scratch the client.
Jewelry that interferes with massage.
Anything on the hands that compromises hygiene or comfort.

sections.title: 9. Face and General Presentation
paragraphs: The therapist should maintain a clean, neat and professional facial appearance.
Where makeup is worn, it should be appropriate for the spa environment.
The objective is not to require a particular beauty style. The objective is: Clean. Presentable. Professional.
The therapist should appear awake, alert and ready for work rather than visibly disorganized or poorly prepared.

sections.title: 10. Footwear Standard
paragraphs: Footwear should be clean, appropriate for the spa, comfortable for movement, safe on treatment-room floors, quiet enough not to disturb clients unnecessarily, and free from offensive odour.
Therapists should not wear footwear that makes excessive noise while walking around a relaxing massage environment.

sections.title: 11. Accessories Standard
paragraphs: Accessories should be minimal, safe, practical, and professional.
Anything that can affect client comfort should be removed before massage.
list: Large bracelets.
Noisy jewelry.
Sharp rings.
Accessories that can scratch clients.
Items that repeatedly interfere with massage movements.
Excessive accessories that distract from the professional appearance.

sections.title: 12. Appearance Check Procedure
paragraphs: Before becoming available for clients, every therapist should conduct a brief personal appearance check.

sections.title: Step 1 — Check the Uniform
paragraphs: Ask: Is it clean? Is it properly worn? Is it wrinkled excessively? Is there a visible stain? Does it smell fresh? Is anything torn or damaged?
Correct any problem before receiving a client.

sections.title: Step 2 — Check Hair
paragraphs: Ensure hair is neat, hair is controlled, long hair is properly secured where necessary, and hair will not repeatedly fall on the client.

sections.title: Step 3 — Check Personal Hygiene
paragraphs: Confirm body is fresh, underarms are clean, deodorant has been used, there is no strong body odour, and feet and footwear are fresh.
Where necessary, complete the Freshen-Up Routine.

sections.title: Step 4 — Check Breath
paragraphs: Before beginning client interaction: confirm breath is fresh, brush or use mouthwash where necessary, and use an appropriate mint if needed.

sections.title: Step 5 — Check Hands and Nails
paragraphs: Inspect palms, fingers, fingernails, and nail edges. Ensure nothing can scratch or inconvenience the client.

sections.title: Step 6 — Check Accessories
paragraphs: Remove anything that may scratch the client, make noise, interfere with massage, or become uncomfortable during the session.

sections.title: Step 7 — Check Footwear
paragraphs: Ensure footwear is clean, properly worn, suitable for work, and free from offensive odour.

sections.title: Step 8 — Final Mirror Check
paragraphs: Before becoming client-ready, look at your overall presentation.
Ask: "If I were the client meeting this therapist for the first time, would this appearance give me confidence?"
If the answer is no, correct the issue before attending to the client.

sections.title: 13. What Good Appearance Looks Like
paragraphs: A therapist meeting the Zura Spa Appearance Standard should appear fresh, clean, neat, well groomed, properly dressed, professionally presented, and ready for work.
The client should not be distracted by hair, smell, clothing, nails, shoes, breath, or accessories.
Professional appearance should almost disappear into the experience because nothing about it makes the client uncomfortable.

sections.title: 14. What the Opposite Looks Like
paragraphs: The opposite of the Zura Spa Appearance Standard is a therapist who appears untidy, unwashed, unprepared, careless, neglected, inappropriately dressed, or poorly groomed.

sections.title: Dirty or Smelly Uniform
paragraphs: A uniform that is stained, sweaty, smelly, excessively wrinkled, damaged, or improperly worn communicates carelessness before the massage begins.

sections.title: Poor Personal Hygiene
paragraphs: This includes noticeable body odour, dirty underarms, dirty hands, dirty nails, offensive foot odour, and strong stale sweat smell.

sections.title: Bad Breath
paragraphs: Because therapists communicate closely with clients, poor oral hygiene can immediately make the experience uncomfortable.

sections.title: Untidy Hair
paragraphs: Hair repeatedly falling onto the therapist's face, the massage bed, the client, or massage oil creates both a professionalism and hygiene concern.

sections.title: Unsafe Nails or Jewelry
paragraphs: Long nails, sharp nails or unsuitable jewelry can scratch the client, cause discomfort, and interrupt massage movements.

sections.title: Excessive Fragrance
paragraphs: A therapist may be clean but use so much perfume that the client finds it uncomfortable. Some clients may also be sensitive to strong fragrances.

sections.title: Inappropriate Footwear
paragraphs: Dirty, noisy or unsuitable footwear can affect safety, hygiene, client relaxation, and professional presentation.

sections.title: Looking Unprepared
paragraphs: A therapist arriving for the client while fixing their hair, adjusting clothing, looking for shoes, freshening breath in front of the client, or trying to clean stains from the uniform communicates that they were not ready.

sections.title: 15. Why Zura Spa Will Not Tolerate Poor Appearance
paragraphs: Poor appearance cannot be treated as merely "That is how the therapist chooses to look." Once a therapist is representing Zura Spa and attending to clients, appearance becomes a professional issue.
Zura Spa will not normalize persistent poor appearance because it affects hygiene, client confidence, client comfort, brand reputation, team discipline, and the perceived quality of the service.
A therapist may perform an excellent massage and still create a poor experience if the client is distracted by strong body odour, dirty hands, long scratching nails, bad breath, or dirty clothing.
The massage experience involves the whole therapist, not just their massage technique.

sections.title: 16. Impact of Poor Appearance on the Client
paragraphs: Poor appearance can cause a client to think: "Is this hygienic?" "Are these sheets clean?" "Was this room properly prepared?" "Is this spa professionally managed?"

This can reduce the client's ability to relax. It can also cause discomfort during close contact, loss of confidence, complaints, shortened sessions, requests for another therapist, negative reviews, failure to return, and negative word of mouth.
A client should never have to tolerate an unpleasant hygiene condition because they do not want to embarrass the therapist.

sections.title: 17. Impact on the Team
paragraphs: Poor appearance does not affect only the therapist involved. It affects the team.

sections.title: It Damages the Shared Brand
paragraphs: A client may not say "That particular therapist was untidy." They may say "Zura Spa therapists are untidy." One person's appearance can therefore affect everyone's reputation.

sections.title: It Creates Unequal Standards
paragraphs: Therapists who consistently prepare properly, wash, iron uniforms, groom themselves, and maintain hygiene may become frustrated when another therapist repeatedly ignores the same standards without consequence.

sections.title: It Weakens Discipline
paragraphs: If poor appearance is repeatedly tolerated, other therapists may begin thinking: "Apparently this standard is optional." Small compromises gradually become the new normal.

sections.title: It Places Extra Responsibility on Colleagues
paragraphs: Other team members may need to remind the therapist repeatedly, delay client allocation, find replacement uniforms, find another therapist, handle complaints, or cover a session. One therapist's lack of preparation can therefore create unnecessary work for others.

sections.title: It Can Affect Client Allocation
paragraphs: If management cannot confidently assign a therapist because of their presentation, other therapists may receive additional workload.

sections.title: It Can Cause Embarrassment to Co-Therapists
paragraphs: During a 4-hands massage, both therapists represent the service together. If one therapist has poor hygiene or presentation, the client's dissatisfaction may affect both therapists. The professional therapist can therefore suffer because of the co-therapist's lack of preparation.

sections.title: 18. Appearance Is a Team Standard
paragraphs: Team members should help maintain the standard respectfully.

If a colleague has a stain, an issue with their uniform, something in their hair, or a hygiene concern they may not realize, it is better to tell them privately and respectfully than allow them to attend to a client unaware.
However, colleagues should not have to repeatedly remind the same therapist about basic grooming responsibilities. Every therapist is primarily responsible for their own appearance.

sections.title: 19. What Therapists Should Do
list: Bathe and arrive fresh.
Wear clean uniforms.
Iron or properly prepare uniforms.
Maintain neat hair.
Secure hair where necessary.
Use deodorant.
Maintain fresh breath.
Keep hands clean.
Keep nails short and smooth.
Maintain clean footwear.
Use fragrance moderately.
Remove unsuitable jewelry.
Check themselves before the first client.
Freshen up during the day when necessary.
Change a dirty uniform where necessary.
Maintain the standard throughout the shift.
Respond immediately when an appearance issue is pointed out.

sections.title: 20. What Therapists Should Not Do
list: Report for client duties visibly unwashed.
Wear dirty uniforms.
Wear uniforms with strong body odour.
Wear badly damaged uniforms without reporting the issue.
Attend to a client while excessively sweaty without freshening up.
Attempt to cover strong body odour with perfume alone.
Use overpowering perfume.
Attend to a client with poor breath hygiene.
Massage with visibly dirty hands.
Keep nails long enough to scratch the client.
Massage with sharp or broken nails.
Wear jewelry that can scratch the client.
Allow hair to repeatedly fall onto the client's body.
Continually touch or adjust hair during massage.
Wear inappropriate or dirty footwear.
Wear noisy footwear that repeatedly disrupts relaxation.
Arrive for the client while still getting dressed.
Begin fixing personal appearance in front of the client.
Ignore feedback about hygiene or grooming.
Respond defensively when respectfully informed about an appearance concern.
Depend on colleagues to constantly remind them to maintain basic hygiene.
Assume that being good at massage makes appearance unimportant.
Follow the appearance standard only when management is present.

sections.title: 21. Appearance Concerns and Correction
paragraphs: An appearance issue does not need to become an embarrassing situation.
Where possible, correction should be private, respectful, immediate, and practical.
Examples: "Please freshen up before your next session." or "Your uniform has become stained. Please change before taking another client."
The objective is to correct the issue before it affects the client.
However, where the same appearance or hygiene problem continues after repeated correction, it becomes more than an accidental issue. It becomes a failure to maintain the professional standard.

sections.title: 22. Appearance and Accountability
paragraphs: At Zura Spa: An accidental stain + immediate correction = normal workplace issue. Sweating + proper freshening up = responsible behaviour. A grooming issue + accepting correction = professional response.
But: Repeated poor hygiene + no effort to improve = performance concern. Repeatedly attending clients while improperly presented = disciplinary concern.
The expectation is not perfection. The expectation is reasonable preparation, consistent hygiene and willingness to correct an issue immediately.

sections.title: 23. The Zura Spa Appearance Standard
paragraphs: CLEAN → CHECK → GROOM → FRESHEN → DRESS → PRESENT → MAINTAIN

Every therapist should be able to answer YES before attending to a client: Am I clean? Is my uniform clean? Does my uniform smell fresh? Is my hair neat? Is my breath fresh? Are my hands clean? Are my nails safe? Are my shoes clean? Do I smell fresh without being overpowering? Do I look ready to professionally attend to a client?
If the answer to any important question is NO, correct it before the session.
Looking good is not the entire standard. Looking clean, professional and client-ready is.
Good massage skills cannot compensate for poor hygiene.
Professional appearance is not optional because the client experiences it directly.
Your appearance speaks before your hands do.
LOOK PROFESSIONAL. STAY FRESH. REPRESENT THE STANDARD. SERVE PROFESSIONALLY.

remember: Your appearance speaks before your hands do. Look professional, stay fresh, and represent the standard.
